formal_statement: ∀ (n q M B : ℕ) (w : (Fin n → Bool) → List Bool), 0 < q → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.QueryLocal n q w → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (w x).length ≤ M) → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin n => x i = true).card % 2 = 1 ↔ w x ∈ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.PartialMCSP) → (∀ (n' s : ℕ) (T : List (Option Bool)), w (fun _ : Fin n => false) = List.replicate s true ++ false :: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.encodePartial T → T.length = 2 ^ n' → ∃ f : (Fin n' → Bool) → Bool, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Consistent n' T f ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize n' f B) → 2 * q * (Nat.log 2 M + 2) < n → 2 ^ ((n - 3 * q) / (4 * q)) ≤ 8 * q * (B * (B * ((3 * ((Nat.log 2 M + B + 1) * (Nat.log 2 M + B + 1))) ^ (B - 1) * (Nat.log 2 M + B))))
plain_statement: CONJECTURE, a corollary of L-meta-030, not found stated in print: if a q-local map (QueryLocal) with outputs of length at most M reduces parity on n bits to partial MCSP, 2q(log2 M + 2) < n, and the partial table it outputs on the all-false input has a consistent circuit of size B, then 2^((n-3q)/(4q)) is at most 8q B^2 (3 (log2 M + B + 1)^2)^(B-1) (log2 M + B). Extends the method of the 2017 local reduction theorem for MCSP (Murray and Williams, Theory of Computing 13) to partial MCSP.
title: No q-local reduction of parity to partial MCSP with a simple zero-input table, unless n is small (finite form)
